title: OpenAI Response mismatch inventory and mitigation playbook
creator: Ava Chen
description: Catalog behavioral mismatches surfaced when mapping OpenAI Responses protocol events to Redwood's Responses model. Focus areas: streaming event ordering and partial payloads, tool/function-call framing differences (argument encoding, chunk boundaries, idempotency), and structured-output framing (JSON streaming, bracket-splitting, closing-token heuristics). Goal: produce a prioritized mitigation playbook with per-gap runtime fallback policies, contract tests, and canary gating for console/SDK surface changes.
acceptance_criteria: Comprehensive taxonomy of observed mismatches with reproducible repro steps and minimal test inputs
Mitigation proposals for top 6 high-impact mismatches including runtime changes and contract tests
Automated contract test harness integrated into CI that simulates streaming truncation and chunked function-call args
Rollout plan with canary metrics (error-rate, toolcall-failure-rate, new-issue regression delta) and console dashboard cards
Docs/SDK change notes and a migration playbook for customers relying on OpenAI Responses semantics
implementation_notes: Phase 1: Fast inventory (2w) — run corpus of recorded customer traffic and synthetic fuzz inputs through existing translation layer, capture event diffs and token-level provenance
Phase 2: Pattern classification — group mismatches into classes: ordering, truncation, framing, metadata loss, type coercion, and tool idempotency
Phase 3: Mitigations — for each class propose one of: runtime adapter tweak, preflight sanitizer, post-emit reconciler, or policy-based fallback to compatibility model
Prefer non-breaking runtime heuristics with opt-out flags; only change SDKs if necessary and coordinate deprecation windows
Add contract tests that use deterministic seeded LLM outputs (recorded from upstream short-lived variant) so CI is stable
Measure canary using synthetic workload and two real customer tenants (opt-in) to capture true customer surface regressions
notes: 2025-02-12: Ticket created after on-call incident where a customer observed function-call args being split across streaming frames, causing JSON.parse failures in their handler. Linked incident postmortem: https://redwood.atlassian.net/l/cp/INC-9839

2025-02-18: Initial inventory run completed against 4M streaming events corpus. Found 7 recurring patterns. Raw diff artifacts uploaded: https://drive.redwood.ai/shared/responses-inventory-20250218.zip

2025-02-21: Design review with API/SDK team. Decision: introduce a streaming framing validator in runtime to enforce at-most-one top-level open-bracket per event and to synthesize a stable chunk boundary token in ambiguous cases. Action item assigned to ENG-27901 for prototype.

2025-02-26: Early prototype for chunk-reassembler pushed (PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/1289). Prototype handles bracket-splitting for small payloads but adds ~1.2ms median latency in microbenchmarks. Trade-off: improved client compatibility vs small latency cost. Captured perf delta dashboard: https://dash.redwood.ai/d/runtime/streaming-framing

2025-03-01: Security review call — KMS/PII considerations for logging recovered toolcall payloads. Decided to redact full argument values from debug logs by default and only keep hash+length. Follow-up: add config flag redact_tool_inputs = true (ENG-28344)

2025-03-04: Sprint checkpoint: prioritized fixes and canary plan drafted. Top-3 mitigations to implement first: (1) chunk-reassembler with budgeted buffering, (2) toolcall idempotency token propagation for retries, (3) structured-output tolerant parser with strict mode behind feature flag. Canary will target dedicated capacity tenants and two small hosted customers. Canary run plan: 2% traffic -> 10% -> 50% over 3 days with rollback if toolcall-error-rate increases > 0.5%

Review feedback: PM asked to include migration notes for customers using streaming parsers tied to token offsets. Design suggested instrumenting 'token-provenance' header in runtime responses (opt-in). Engineering flagged potential spec drift and suggested preferring shared contract tests instead of adding new headers until stabilization.

Next steps: Implement chunk-reassembler PR with benchmarking and opt-in feature-flag; build contract test harness (python + node) that simulates chunked frames and function-call fragmentation; draft migration guide for customers; schedule canary in 2025-03-18 window.
